This occupational video-observation study shows parameter- and categorization-specific agreement; it does not invalidate all visual examination or establish clinical meaning.
- Steven J. Obst et al., “Three-Dimensional Deformation and Transverse Rotation of the Human Free Achilles Tendon In Vivo during Isometric Plantarflexion Contraction,” *Journal of Applied Physiology* 116, no. 4 (2014): 376–384, [doi:10.1152/japplphysiol.01249.2013](https://doi.org/10.1152/japplphysiol.01249.2013). Eight participants were imaged at rest and 70% maximal voluntary isometric contraction. Use for heterogeneous three-dimensional tendon deformation; not injury, adaptation, or a preferred rotation.
- Sundar Srinivasan et al., “Low-Magnitude Mechanical Loading Becomes Osteogenic When Rest Is Inserted between Each Load Cycle,” *Journal of Bone and Mineral Research* 17, no. 9 (2002): 1613–1620, [doi:10.1359/jbmr.2002.17.9.1613](https://doi.org/10.1359/jbmr.2002.17.9.1613). Avian-ulna and mouse-tibia models showed a substantially different periosteal response when ten-second rests were inserted. Use for sequence, rest, and site specificity; not a human exercise prescription.
- Sungwoo Park and James M. Finley, [“Manual Stabilization Reveals a Transient Role for Balance Control during Locomotor Adaptation,”](https://doi.org/10.1152/jn.00377.2021) *Journal of Neurophysiology* 128, no. 4 (2022): 808–818. Twenty-four healthy young adults adapted to split-belt walking with or without handrail contact. The study supports segmental contributions to whole-body angular momentum and environment-dependent early adaptation, not a durable preferred configuration.
- T. M. Quinn, R. G. Allen, B. J. Schalet, P. Perumbuli, and E. B. Hunziker, “Matrix and Cell Injury Due to Sub-Impact Loading of Adult Bovine Articular Cartilage Explants: Effects of Strain Rate and Peak Stress,” *Journal of Orthopaedic Research* 19, no. 2 (2001): 242–249, [doi:10.1016/S0736-0266(00)00025-5](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0736-0266%2800%2900025-5). The study supports rate-, peak-stress-, and region-dependent injury under its bovine-explant protocol, not a human walking threshold, osteoarthritis cause, or symptom relation.
- Tammy C. Hoffmann et al., “Better Reporting of Interventions: Template for Intervention Description and Replication (TIDieR) Checklist and Guide,” *BMJ* 348 (2014): g1687, [doi:10.1136/bmj.g1687](https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.g1687). Reproducible description does not establish safety, efficacy, mechanism, or applicability.
- Tammy L. Haut Donahue, Maury L. Hull, M. M. Rashid, and Christopher R. Jacobs, “The Sensitivity of Tibiofemoral Contact Pressure to the Size and Shape of the Lateral and Medial Menisci,” *Journal of Orthopaedic Research* 22, no. 4 (2004): 807–814, [doi:10.1016/j.orthres.2003.12.010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.orthres.2003.12.010). This finite-element geometry-perturbation study supports conditional sensitivity of modeled contact variables to meniscal size and shape. It does not supply a living response or biological tolerance threshold.
- Tatiane da Silva et al., “Recurrence of Low Back Pain Is Common: A Prospective Inception Cohort Study,” *Journal of Physiotherapy* 65, no. 3 (2019): 159–165, [doi:10.1016/j.jphys.2019.04.010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jphys.2019.04.010). The twelve-month recurrence estimates among 250 recently recovered people depended on outcome definition and do not supply a mechanism or individual forecast.
- Taylor Shockey, Toni Alterman, Haiou Yang, and Ming-Lun Lu, “Workplace Psychosocial Factors, Work Organization, and Physical Exertion as Risk Factors for Low Back Pain among US Workers,” *Journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine* 66, no. 6 (2024): 467–474, [doi:10.1097/JOM.0000000000003087](https://doi.org/10.1097/JOM.0000000000003087). The analysis used cross-sectional self-report data from 17,464 employed adults. It does not establish temporal or causal assignment; formal interactions with physical exertion were not statistically significant.
- Teresa Y. L. Liu-Ambrose et al., “Both Resistance and Agility Training Increase Cortical Bone Density in 75- to 85-Year-Old Women with Low Bone Mass: A 6-Month Randomized Controlled Trial,” *Journal of Clinical Densitometry* 7, no. 4 (2004): 390–398, [doi:10.1385/JCD:7:4:390](https://doi.org/10.1385/JCD:7:4:390). The prospective intervention lasted twenty-five weeks. Use for small, site-specific positive changes amid many null bone outcomes; not general exercise efficacy.
- Tessa Hart et al., [“A Theory-Driven System for the Specification of Rehabilitation Treatments,”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apmr.2018.09.109) *Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation* 100, no. 1 (2019): 172–180. The article supports an existing cross-diagnostic rehabilitation framework separating targets, ingredients, hypothesized mechanisms, and distal aims; it specifies interventions rather than reconstructing mechanical exposure histories.
- Tetsuhiro Iguchi et al., “Lumbar Instability and Clinical Symptoms: Which Is the More Critical Factor for Symptoms: Sagittal Translation or Segment Angulation?,” *Journal of Spinal Disorders & Techniques* 17, no. 4 (2004): 284–290, [doi:10.1097/01.bsd.0000102473.95064.9d](https://doi.org/10.1097/01.bsd.0000102473.95064.9d). The observational flexion-extension study involved 1,090 symptomatic outpatients. Its thresholds and associations are study-specific and do not establish causal origin.
- Theresa Foti, Jon R. Davids, and Anita Bagley, [“A Biomechanical Analysis of Gait during Pregnancy,”](https://doi.org/10.2106/00004623-200005000-00003) *Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery. American Volume* 82, no. 5 (2000): 625–632. Fifteen women were studied late in pregnancy and one year postpartum. The result supports bounded kinematic, kinetic, and individual comparisons, not a universal pregnancy posture or corrective strategy.
- Thomas A. Hutchins et al., “ACR Appropriateness Criteria® Low Back Pain: 2021 Update,” *Journal of the American College of Radiology* 18, no. 11S (2021): S361–S379, [doi:10.1016/j.jacr.2021.08.002](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacr.2021.08.002); see also the American College of Radiology’s [official scenario tables and narrative](https://acsearch.acr.org/docs/69483/Narrative/). The source supports condition- and scenario-specific imaging appropriateness. It is not a comprehensive current low-back-pain guideline or evidence that one finding is causal.
- Thomas J. Roberts and Emanuel Azizi, [“Flexible Mechanisms: The Diverse Roles of Biological Springs in Vertebrate Movement,”](https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.038588) *Journal of Experimental Biology* 214, no. 3 (2011): 353–361. The review supports energy storage and return, power attenuation, and other state- and task-dependent muscle–tendon functions; it does not establish one body-wide tissue sequence.
- Thomas J. Roberts and Emanuel Azizi, [“Flexible Mechanisms: The Diverse Roles of Biological Springs in Vertebrate Movement,”](https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.038588) *Journal of Experimental Biology* 214, no. 3 (2011): 353–361; Nicolai Konow, Emanuel Azizi, and Thomas J. Roberts, [“Muscle Power Attenuation by Tendon during Energy Dissipation,”](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspb.2011.1435) *Proceedings of the Royal Society B* 279, no. 1731 (2012): 1108–1113; Chavaunne T. Thorpe et al., [“Specialization of Tendon Mechanical Properties Results from Interfascicular Differences,”](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsif.2012.0362) *Journal of the Royal Society Interface* 9, no. 76 (2012): 3108–3117. The experiments were nonhuman and task- or tendon-specific; they do not establish a universal human energy or protection rule.
- Thomas Lange et al., [“Quantification of Patellofemoral Cartilage Deformation and Contact Area Changes in Response to Static Loading via High-Resolution MRI with Prospective Motion Correction,”](https://doi.org/10.1002/jmri.26724) *Journal of Magnetic Resonance Imaging* 50, no. 5 (2019): 1561–1570. The study supports load-dependent contact-area and cartilage-thickness changes in fifteen healthy male participants. It does not provide a complete pressure field, harmful threshold, or clinical conclusion.
- Tina T. Chowdhury, David L. Bader, and David A. Lee, “Dynamic Compression Inhibits the Synthesis of Nitric Oxide and PGE2 by IL-1β-Stimulated Chondrocytes Cultured in Agarose Constructs,” *Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications* 285, no. 5 (2001): 1168–1174, [doi:10.1006/bbrc.2001.5311](https://doi.org/10.1006/bbrc.2001.5311). Primary bovine articular chondrocytes in agarose were exposed to 15% dynamic compression at 1 Hz for forty-eight hours. Use for a mechanical–inflammatory-state interaction at cell-culture scale; not an exercise, disease, or treatment conclusion.
- Tsutomu Fukui, Yasuhisa Ueda, and Fumiko Kamijo, [“Ankle, Knee, and Hip Joint Contribution to Body Support during Gait,”](https://doi.org/10.1589/jpts.28.2834) *Journal of Physical Therapy Science* 28, no. 10 (2016): 2834–2837. The study involved twenty-five healthy adults and supports phase-dependent, covarying net joint-moment contributions during walking. It does not identify unique muscle forces or a preferred joint strategy.
- TU Delft OpenCourseWare, [“Main Takeaways on Load Paths,”](https://ocw.tudelft.nl/course-readings/4-2-4-main-takeaways-on-load-paths/) in *Introduction to Aerospace Structures and Materials*, accessed July 11, 2026. The course supplies the bounded structural meaning linking an applied load to equilibrium forces. This book's multicarrier biological extension is explicitly a project-defined model.
- Tyler J. VanderWeele, “Mediation Analysis: A Practitioner's Guide,” *Annual Review of Public Health* 37 (2016): 17–32, [doi:10.1146/annurev-publhealth-032315-021402](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-publhealth-032315-021402). The guide supports the assumptions and distinct questions involved in direct and indirect effects; measuring a post-treatment variable does not by itself establish a mechanism.
- U.S. Food and Drug Administration and National Institutes of Health, [BEST Resource Taxonomy](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-resources/best-resource-taxonomy) and [Patient-Focused Drug Development Glossary](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-approval-process-drugs/patient-focused-drug-development-glossary), living official resources accessed July 11, 2026. These resources support distinctions among biomarkers and patient-, clinician-, observer-, and performance-based assessments. Their regulatory terminology does not validate any Book I measure.
- U.S. Food and Drug Administration, [*Assessing the Credibility of Computational Modeling and Simulation in Medical Device Submissions*](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/assessing-credibility-computational-modeling-and-simulation-medical-device-submissions), final guidance, November 2023. The guidance supports context of use, model risk, and credibility evidence proportional to decision consequence. It does not validate a knee or spine model used in this chapter.
- United Nations, *Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities*, Article 2, “Definitions,” [official text](https://www.un.org/development/desa/disabilities/convention-on-the-rights-of-persons-with-disabilities/article-2-definitions.html). The definitions distinguish universal design, accommodation, and assistive devices; they are not intervention-effect estimates.
- Valter Devecchi, Deborah Falla, Hélio V. Cabral, Jacques Abboud, Paul Hodges, and Alessio Gallina, [“Direction Matters: A Crossover Study on Motor Adaptations to Movement-Evoked Pain Induced in the Lumbar Region,”](https://doi.org/10.1002/ejp.70142) *European Journal of Pain* 29, no. 10 (2025): e70142. The experiment involved thirty healthy adults and supports direction-specific adaptation to experimentally imposed pain, not the origin or treatment of chronic pain.
- Vasco V. Mascarenhas et al., [“Hip Shape Is Symmetric, Non-Dependent on Limb Dominance and Gender-Specific: Implications for Femoroacetabular Impingement. A 3D CT Analysis in Asymptomatic Subjects,”](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00330-017-5072-9) *European Radiology* 28, no. 4 (2018): 1609–1624. The study supports broad morphology distributions and frequent threshold-crossing findings in an asymptomatic sample. It does not show that morphology never matters.
- Verena J. M. M. Schrier et al., [“Reliability of Ultrasound Speckle Tracking with Singular Value Decomposition for Quantifying Displacement in the Carpal Tunnel,”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbiomech.2019.01.022) *Journal of Biomechanics* 85 (2019): 141–147; Jan-Wiebe H. Korstanje et al., [“Ultrasonographic Assessment of Flexor Tendon Mobilization: Effect of Different Protocols on Tendon Excursion,”](https://doi.org/10.2106/JBJS.J.01521) *Journal of Bone and Joint Surgery. American Volume* 94, no. 5 (2012): 394–402. The studies used different structures, locations, tasks, and protocols. Their values should not be pooled into a context-free normal range.
- Victoria Joppin et al., “Towards a Better Understanding of Abdominal Wall Biomechanics: In Vivo Relationship between Dynamic Intra-Abdominal Pressure and Magnetic Resonance Imaging Measurements,” *Clinical Biomechanics* 121 (2025): 106396, [doi:10.1016/j.clinbiomech.2024.106396](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinbiomech.2024.106396). Eighteen healthy participants completed breathing, coughing, and Valsalva tasks with dynamic magnetic resonance imaging and an ingestible pressure sensor. The study supports participant-, task-, and region-specific pressure–displacement relations, not a universal compliance or clinical threshold.
- Viviane Otoni do Carmo Carvalhais et al., [“Myofascial Force Transmission between the Latissimus Dorsi and Gluteus Maximus Muscles: An In Vivo Experiment,”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jbiomech.2012.11.044) *Journal of Biomechanics* 46, no. 5 (2013): 1003–1007. The 37-participant experiment measured contralateral hip resting position and passive-stiffness endpoints rather than fascial force, so it cannot isolate a carrier or establish a whole-chain relation.
- Waleed Brinjikji et al., “MRI Findings of Disc Degeneration Are More Prevalent in Adults with Low Back Pain than in Asymptomatic Controls: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis,” *AJNR American Journal of Neuroradiology* 36, no. 12 (2015): 2394–2399, [doi:10.3174/ajnr.A4498](https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A4498). Group associations and heterogeneous nulls do not identify an individual pain source, route, or chronology.
- Waleed Brinjikji et al., “Systematic Literature Review of Imaging Features of Spinal Degeneration in Asymptomatic Populations,” *American Journal of Neuroradiology* 36, no. 4 (2015): 811–816, [doi:10.3174/ajnr.A4173](https://doi.org/10.3174/ajnr.A4173). Use for common age-dependent imaging findings without symptoms; not proof that any individual finding is irrelevant.
- William M. Kier, [“The Diversity of Hydrostatic Skeletons,”](https://doi.org/10.1242/jeb.056549) *Journal of Experimental Biology* 215, no. 8 (2012): 1247–1257. Hydrostatic skeletons provide a biological existence proof for pressure-, wall-, muscle-, and geometry-mediated support without rigid elements. The chapter does not transfer a particular invertebrate mechanism to a human cavity.
- World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe, *Screening Programmes: A Short Guide. Increase Effectiveness, Maximize Benefits and Minimize Harm* (Copenhagen: WHO Regional Office for Europe, 2020), ISBN 978-92-8-905478-2, [official publication](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789289054782). The policy guide does not specify diagnosis or validate the seven questions.
- World Health Organization, [“Rehabilitation”](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rehabilitation), fact sheet dated April 22, 2024. The fact sheet supports attention to functioning, disability, environment, person-centered goals, multidisciplinary rehabilitation, and complementarity with medical and surgical interventions. It does not establish the novelty or utility of load routing.
- World Health Organization, [“Social Determinants of Health”](https://www.who.int/health-topics/social-determinants-of-health), official topic page, accessed July 11, 2026. The framework identifies conditions of birth, growth, living, work, aging, and access to power, money, and resources as population-health context, not as an individual causal assignment.
- World Health Organization, [*Framework for Action on Interprofessional Education and Collaborative Practice*](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/framework-for-action-on-interprofessional-education-collaborative-practice), WHO/HRH/HPN/10.3 (2010). The framework supports interprofessional collaboration as a health-system strategy; it does not establish professional hierarchy or validate a routing vocabulary.
- World Health Organization, [“International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF),”](https://www.who.int/classifications/international-classification-of-functioning-disability-and-health) and [*ICF Beginner’s Guide: Towards a Common Language for Functioning, Disability and Health*](https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/icf-beginner-s-guide-towards-a-common-language-for-functioning-disability-and-health) (2002). The ICF supplies an integrative classification framework for body function and structure, activity, participation, and environmental context; it is not evidence for the etiology or causal priority of a mechanical relation.
- World Health Organization, *Health Literacy Development for the Prevention and Control of Noncommunicable Diseases, Volume 2: A Globally Relevant Perspective* (Geneva: World Health Organization, 2022), [official publication](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240055353). The framework supports a socially situated account of literacy, not the validity or effectiveness of the mechanical-literacy construct proposed here.
- World Health Organization, “Health Literacy,” fact sheet updated December 22, 2025, [WHO](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/health-literacy). The framing supports shared personal and organizational responsibility; it does not establish the effectiveness of this book's vocabulary.
- World Health Organization, “Health Technology Assessment,” [WHO health topic](https://www.who.int/health-topics/health-technology-assessment). The policy frame does not show that any proposed biomechanical technology or system change has value.
- World Health Organization, [“International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF),”](https://www.who.int/classifications/international-classification-of-functioning-disability-and-health) official classification and framework, accessed July 11, 2026. The framework supports treating functioning and disability as interactions among health conditions and contextual factors, including environment, activity, and participation; it is not a biomechanical constitutive model.
- World Health Organization, *WHO Guideline for Non-Surgical Management of Chronic Primary Low Back Pain in Adults in Primary and Community Care Settings* (Geneva: World Health Organization, 2023), [official publication](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240081789). The guideline supplies the chronic-primary and person-centered biopsychosocial context; it does not establish the cause of the hypothetical or authorize treatment guidance in this chapter.
- World Health Organization, *WHO Guidelines on Ethical Issues in Public Health Surveillance* (Geneva: World Health Organization, 2017), [official publication](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241512657). The guidance supplies general ethical duties, not workplace-specific legal advice or proof that a selected program is effective.
- World Health Organization, *WHO Policy on Disability* (Geneva: World Health Organization, 2021), [official publication](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240020627); World Health Organization and UNICEF, *Global Report on Assistive Technology* (Geneva: World Health Organization and UNICEF, 2022), [official publication](https://www.who.int/southeastasia/publications/i/item/9789240049451). These sources establish inclusion and access obligations, not the efficacy of any particular educational, mechanical, or ergonomic intervention.
- World Physiotherapy, [“What Is Physiotherapy?”](https://world.physio/resources/what-is-physiotherapy), official professional description accessed July 11, 2026. The source supports movement, function, whole-person context, examination, clinical judgment, intervention, outcome, and referral as established physiotherapy territory. Roles and legal scope vary by jurisdiction.
- Xavier Demondion et al., “Thoracic Outlet: Assessment with MR Imaging in Asymptomatic and Symptomatic Populations,” *Radiology* 227, no. 2 (2003): 461–468, [doi:10.1148/radiol.2272012111](https://doi.org/10.1148/radiol.2272012111). This historical positional protocol compared thirty-five asymptomatic volunteers with fifty-four symptomatic patients; venous compression under the protocol is not thrombotic-venous attribution.
- Xiaohan Xu et al., [“Distinct Patterns in Neuromuscular Adaptation to Repeated Perturbations in Chronic Ankle Instability,”](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12984-025-01838-y) *Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation* 23 (2026): 21. Published online December 12, 2025; official volume citation 2026. Twenty-three participants with chronic ankle instability and twenty-three controls; the study supports repeated-task adaptation and group-specific co-contraction patterns, not injury causation or a treatment directive.
- Xiaohong Jia, Shuangfu Suo, Fan Meng, and Rencheng Wang, [“Effects of Alignment on Interface Pressure for Transtibial Amputee during Walking,”](https://doi.org/10.1080/17483100802044634) *Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology* 3, no. 6 (2008): 339–343. One participant completed three sagittal alignment conditions. The study supports separating peak pressure, duration, and time–pressure integral; it does not establish clinical harm or fitting guidance.
- Y. X. Liu, Stavros Thomopoulos, Victor Birman, J.-S. Li, and Guy M. Genin, [“Bi-Material Attachment through a Compliant Interfacial System at the Tendon-to-Bone Insertion Site,”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mechmat.2011.08.005) *Mechanics of Materials* 44 (2012): 83–92. The idealized optimization supports dependence of selected stress concentrations on spatially varied anisotropic material properties. It is not a measured living field.
- Yao-Wei Shih et al., “Effects of Positive and Negative Expectations on Human Pain Perception Engage Separate but Interrelated and Dependently Regulated Cerebral Mechanisms,” *Journal of Neuroscience* 39, no. 7 (2019): 1261–1274, [doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2154-18.2018](https://doi.org/10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2154-18.2018). This controlled healthy-participant experiment supports expectation-related modulation of pain ratings and neural responses, not tissue origin or disease explanation.
- Yifan Guo, Mohammad R. K. Mofrad, and Adrian B. Tepole, [“On Modeling the Multiscale Mechanobiology of Soft Tissues: Challenges and Progress,”](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0085025) *Biophysics Reviews* 3, no. 3 (2022): 031303. The review supports explicit modeling bridges between hierarchical tissue behavior and cell-scale mechanobiology; it does not make any one internal exposure identifiable from a whole-body task.
- Young-Jo Kim et al., “Mechanical Regulation of Cartilage Biosynthetic Behavior: Physical Stimuli,” *Archives of Biochemistry and Biophysics* 311, no. 1 (1994): 1–12, [doi:10.1006/abbi.1994.1201](https://doi.org/10.1006/abbi.1994.1201). Use for frequency- and region-dependent biosynthesis compared with predicted fluid-flow, pressure, streaming-potential, and cell-deformation fields; the study did not independently manipulate those candidate mechanisms.
- Yuichi Yoshii et al., [“Speckle Tracking Ultrasound for Assessment of the Relative Motion of Flexor Tendon and Subsynovial Connective Tissue in the Human Carpal Tunnel,”](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ultrasmedbio.2009.07.004) *Ultrasound in Medicine & Biology* 35, no. 12 (2009): 1973–1981. The within-person study supports task-dependent tendon excursion, SSCT excursion, and calculated relative motion; it does not identify an ideal task, adverse constraint, or pathological threshold.
- Zina Trost, Christopher R. France, Michael J. Sullivan, and James S. Thomas, “Pain-Related Fear Predicts Reduced Spinal Motion Following Experimental Back Injury,” *Pain* 153, no. 5 (2012): 1015–1021, [doi:10.1016/j.pain.2012.02.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pain.2012.02.001). Fifty-one initially pain-free participants completed reaching before and after induced trunk-extensor soreness. The result is bounded to fear conditional on pain predicting selected motion change.
